profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Microsoft (Mojang Studios)
profile.summary:
As a software engineer by trade and a designer at heart, I have a passion for human-centered computing systems, accessible interactive software, and education technology. In 2020, I graduated from Georgia Tech with a bachelor's degree in Computer Science with a concentration in Media and People and a minor in Industrial Design. I am a software engineer at Microsoft where I have worked on core user experiences for Windows and currently work on client social & messaging features for Minecraft.

Creator of the Party AVL: https://github.com/abrown313/graphics/blob/master/partyavl1.gif

positions.title: Head Undergraduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
From Fall 2019 - Spring 2020, I served as the Head TA for CS 1332.
    • Organized and oversaw a group of 22+ teaching assistants
    • Guest lectured to two sections of 150+ students upon instructor absence
    • Led weekly meetings to coordinate TA and course activity
    • Ensured TAs were taking care of themselves and the students to deliver the best experience as possible

positions.title: Senior Undergraduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
From Summer 2018 - Spring 2019, I served as a Senior TA for CS 1332. This role involved the same responsibilities I had as a regular TA, but with expanded leadership and organizational duties: 
    • Developed teaching guides to be used by all TAs for weekly recitations
    • Wrote questions, reviewed content, and administered exams for the course
    • Worked closely with the instructor to plan and develop an online version of the course
    • Took detailed notes of every lecture for release to students and online course development

positions.title: Undergraduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
As a TA for CS 1332 (Data Structures and Algorithms) taught by Dr. Mary Hudachek-Buswell, I leveraged my experiences to help others and grow my leadership & technical fluency skills.
    • Taught 50 students during a 75-minute, weekly recitation section
    • Reviewed and revised materials to be released to students
    • Graded and provided feedback on exams and homework assignments
    • Held 3 hours of office hours to help students outside of lecture/recitation time

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
During my internship at Microsoft, I worked on the Windows Shell team to prototype a feature that later shipped at "Widgets" on Windows 11.
    • Design and implemented the framework for a new exploratory shell component (C++/CX & XAML)
    • Collaborated with data scientists and designers to prototype a version of the feature for user research (Typescript React)
    • Worked as a part of an intern v-team with a PM, data science, and another SWE intern to fully explore the potential of the feature
positions.insights: Skills: React.js · XAML · User Research · C++

positions.title: Bioinformatics Research Assistant
positions.description:
As a recipient of the School of Biology's "Fast-Track to Research" scholarship, I worked under Dr. Eric Gaucher during my first year of college to study the evolution of Xanthine oxidoreductase.
    • Collected, compiled, and analyzed genomic data to reconstruct ancestral protein sequences
    • Leveraged bioinformatics databases and programs (UniProt, NCBI BLAST, MrBayes, and PAML) to construct phylogenies
    • Attended monthly lab meetings to discuss & present current research findings and collaborating with graduate, doctorate, and post-doctorate students

honors.title: 2019 Undergraduate TA Award
honors.description:
I was nominated by Dr. Mary Hudachek-Buswell for the school-wide Undergraduate TA Award (School of Computer Science) for my outstanding work as a teaching assistant. I won the school-wide award which qualified me for the institute-wide Undergraduate TA Award. I was one of three recipients of the institute-wide Undergraduate TA Award out of around 20 nominees. 

Link: https://ctl.gatech.edu/content/awards
honors.issuer: Issued by Georgia Tech Center for Teaching and Learning (CTL) · Apr 2019

projects.title: The TA Hashboard
projects.description: The Hashboard is a concept conceived by the CS 1332 TA group; it's an office hours dashboard nicknamed the "Hashboard" to match HashMaps, a data structure we teach. The original Hashboard was written by Timothy J. Aveni and was tied heavily to other software tools he wrote. My take on the Hashboard aims to be more modular and easier for future TAs to use once I graduate. The basic functionalities of the Hashboard allow on duty TAs to be loaded and displayed in real time from a Google calendar and allow students to add themselves to a queue for help.

projects.title: Talli
projects.description:
Talli is a web application I worked on in collaboration with five peers and a client, Dr. Jay Lofstead of Sandia National Labs. We designed and implemented a React web application to streamline popular voting at entry-based events. Event organizers can use the app to add their event, sync event entries, manage voting, and tabulate results. Event attendees can join the event voting through a mobile browser, add entries to their ballot, rank their favorites, and submit their ballot.

My Contributions:
• Front end development of event organizer features.
• Logo and user interface design.
• Overseeing and editing design documents produced during development.

Use the app here: https://tallivote.com/
